audits.title: Using the T11 vertebra to minimise the CT-KUB scan field.
audits.standard: Mean percentage overscan length target (value truncated in abstract); overscan >15% defined as excessive; both kidneys fully included
audits.setting: Heartlands, Good Hope and Solihull Hospitals, University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Mean overscan 28.2%; overscan >15% in 94.4%; superior limit at T10 or below in 59%; both kidneys included in 99%.

audits.intervention: New protocol using T11 as the superior scan limit delivered to radiographers.

cycle2.result: Mean overscan 10.6% (SD 4.4%); excessive overscan 35.2%; superior limit at T10 or below in 8%; both kidneys included in 100%.

audits.other_findings: Overscan target was met without compromising scan quality.
audits.citation: Uldin H, McGlynn E, Cleasby M. Using the T11 vertebra to minimise the CT-KUB scan field. Br J Radiol. 2020;93(1110):20190771. doi:10.1259/bjr.20190771. PMID: 32208971.

audits.title: It is time to think inside the (collimation) box; a quality improvement project to reduce over-scanning in CT scanning of the kidneys, ureters and bladder.
audits.standard: RCR: excess CTKUB scan length above the upper pole of the highest kidney should not exceed 10% of total scan length

cycle1.result: Scan length exceeded the standard on 81% of scans (81/100)

audits.intervention: Radiographers viewed image acquisition in real time and manually stopped the scan at the top of the highest kidney
audits.citation: Netke T, Spurr M, Vosough A. It is time to think inside the (collimation) box; a quality improvement project to reduce over-scanning in CT scanning of the kidneys, ureters and bladder. Br J Radiol. 2020;93(1112):20200068. doi:10.1259/bjr.20200068. PMID: 32459517.

audits.title: The proportion of computed tomography kidneys, ureters and bladder (CTKUB) scans that comply with scan extent protocol in an emergency department: a clinical audit and dose ramification study.
audits.standard: Departmental CTKUB scan extent protocol (kidneys to pubic symphysis)
audits.setting: Emergency department, Princess Alexandra Hospital, Brisbane (tertiary hospital)

cycle1.result: Overall compliance in 8 cases (5.3%); 142 (94.7%) non-compliant, commonly over-scanning at the kidneys by 4-5 cm and at the pubic symphysis by 1-2 cm.

audits.other_findings: Phantom simulation estimated dose increases of up to 35% to 45%; a follow-up audit is suggested.
audits.citation: Kasi A, Steffens T, Starkey D, Braithwaite V. The proportion of computed tomography kidneys, ureters and bladder (CTKUB) scans that comply with scan extent protocol in an emergency department: a clinical audit and dose ramification study. J Med Radiat Sci. 2021;68(1):13-20. doi:10.1002/jmrs.451. PMID: 33350603.

audits.standard: Renal CT guidelines: scan limited to the region required; overscanning defined as more than 10% of total scan length above the highest kidney margin

audits.title: Optimizing z-axis coverage in computed tomography scans of the kidney, ureters, and bladder via standard operating procedures: a clinical audit report.
audits.standard: Departmental standard operating procedure: scan from T10 vertebra endplate to inferior margin of pubic symphysis
audits.setting: Radiology department, Regional Hospital Heilig Hart Tienen

cycle1.result: Internal audit identified variability in CT KUB doses and over-scanning.

audits.intervention: Phase 1: new SOP with osseous anatomical landmarks; phase 2: SOP amended to use a sagittal scout view to identify the T10 endplate.

cycle2.result: Phase 1 reduced scan length by 14% and DLP by 32%; phase 2 reduced scan length by a further 7%; overall scan length down 20% and DLP down 55%.

audits.other_findings: 247 CT KUB scans analysed in total.
audits.citation: Blom RM, Cockmartin L, Marshall N, Bosmans H. Optimizing z-axis coverage in computed tomography scans of the kidney, ureters, and bladder via standard operating procedures: a clinical audit report. Radiat Prot Dosimetry. 2025;201(15):1059-1067. doi:10.1093/rpd/ncaf091. PMID: 40794892.

audits.title: Standardized CT KUB Protocols for Nephrolithiasis: A Retrospective Analysis of Radiation Exposure and Cranial Extent Guidelines.
audits.standard: IR(ME)R principle of minimising radiation; local protocol to start CT KUB at the T10-T12 vertebral level (no formal national guideline)
audits.setting: District general hospital, Doncaster Royal Infirmary

cycle1.result: 48% (n=49) of scans started above T10, 51% (n=52) from T10-T12 and 1% below T12; mean effective dose 6.37 mSv above T10 vs 4.56 mSv from T10-T12.

audits.intervention: Findings presented to urology and radiology departments and a new protocol to commence CT KUB from T10-T12 devised.

cycle2.result: 21.9% (n=23) started above T10, 75.2% (n=79) from T10-T12 and 2.9% below T12; mean dose 6.76 mSv above T10 vs 4.12 mSv from T10-T12.

audits.other_findings: Kidneys were fully visualised from T10 in 98.6% of all scans, but from T12 in only 79.2%, supporting T10 as the cranial limit.
audits.citation: Jarral F, Hamdy A, Mohamed G, Mobayen R, Dave N, Eltawil M, et al.. Standardized CT KUB Protocols for Nephrolithiasis: A Retrospective Analysis of Radiation Exposure and Cranial Extent Guidelines. Cureus. 2024;16(12):e75743. doi:10.7759/cureus.75743. PMID: 39687674.
